hyp:logistic_regularization_cv.statement: L2 regularization improves logistic regression generalization via cross-validation; optimal lambda exists within [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0] that minimizes Brier score

gap:interaction_effect_size.statement: Whether polynomial interaction terms (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) meaningfully reduce Brier score compared to raw features in logistic regression

gap:compression_tradeoff.statement: Which sparsity (20-60%) and bit-width (4-8) compression strategy best preserves the dense model's predictive performance

claim:optimal_lambda_0_1.statement: Among L2 regularization strengths [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0], lambda=0.1 minimizes 5-fold CV Brier score (0.2071) with 0.0089 improvement over unregularized baseline (0.2160)

claim:interaction_improves_model.statement: Adding polynomial interaction terms (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) significantly improves logistic regression, with paired t-test t=3.912 (p=0.017) indicating meaningful performance gain; raw Brier=0.2071 vs interaction Brier=0.1814

claim:sparsity20_bits4_best.statement: Among compression strategies, 20% sparsity with 4-bit quantization achieves highest retention (0.9998) of dense model performance, indicating minimal information loss with aggressive compression
